theorems.title: Classical global weak existence
theorems.hypotheses_summary: Finite-energy divergence-free initial data in the classical Leray framework; consult the primary source for the exact approximation and function-space formulation.
theorems.conclusion_summary: Global-in-time weak solutions exist in the Leray sense.
theorems.relation_to_clay: Establishes a weaker global existence theory than the smooth solutions demanded by the global-regularity formulations.

theorems.title: Local strong-solution theory
theorems.hypotheses_summary: Initial data satisfying the source's strong-solution function-space hypotheses.
theorems.conclusion_summary: A unique strong solution exists for a nonzero time interval in the source framework.
theorems.relation_to_clay: Moves the unresolved issue to continuation/global control rather than instantaneous local existence.

theorems.title: Serrin conditional regularity criterion
theorems.hypotheses_summary: A weak solution additionally satisfies a Serrin integrability condition; the standard three-dimensional summary is a mixed space-time condition with 2/q + 3/p <= 1 in the admissible source range, with exact endpoint and locality assumptions taken from the primary source.
theorems.conclusion_summary: Under the additional integrability hypothesis the weak solution is regular in the corresponding region/time interval.
theorems.relation_to_clay: Provides a continuation/regularity target: a global a priori bound in a qualifying Serrin class would be powerful, but the criterion alone does not prove such a bound.

theorems.title: Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg partial regularity
theorems.hypotheses_summary: Suitable weak solutions satisfying the local energy inequality in the Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg framework.
theorems.conclusion_summary: The possible singular set is small; in particular its one-dimensional parabolic Hausdorff measure is zero.
theorems.relation_to_clay: Severely restricts the geometry/size of possible singularities but leaves open whether any singularity occurs.

theorems.title: Critical L3 local and small-data global theory
theorems.hypotheses_summary: Initial data in the critical L3-based framework used by Kato, with a sufficiently small critical norm for the global small-data conclusion.
theorems.conclusion_summary: Local strong well-posedness holds in the critical framework, and sufficiently small critical data give global solutions.
theorems.relation_to_clay: Shows that the unresolved difficulty concerns large-data behavior rather than all critical data indiscriminately.

theorems.title: Small-data global well-posedness in BMO^{-1}
theorems.hypotheses_summary: Divergence-free initial data sufficiently small in the BMO^{-1}-type critical norm of the source framework.
theorems.conclusion_summary: A global well-posed solution exists in the Koch-Tataru solution space.
theorems.relation_to_clay: Extends the region of globally controlled small critical data while preserving the large-data gap.

theorems.title: Endpoint L3 regularity / blow-up criterion
theorems.hypotheses_summary: A suitable/weak solution remains uniformly bounded in the spatial L3 norm up to a candidate singular time, under the source's precise hypotheses.
theorems.conclusion_summary: The endpoint L3 control prevents the candidate finite-time singularity; contrapositively, finite-time blow-up requires loss of the corresponding uniform L3 control.
theorems.relation_to_clay: Provides a sharp necessary blow-up behavior and a critical target for any global a priori estimate.

theorems.title: Exclusion of classical backward self-similar L3 profiles
theorems.hypotheses_summary: Backward self-similar Leray-form solutions whose similarity profile obeys the source's L3/integrability hypotheses.
theorems.conclusion_summary: No nontrivial profile in the stated class yields the proposed backward self-similar blow-up.
theorems.relation_to_clay: Removes an important classical blow-up ansatz from the admissible search space under its hypotheses.

theorems.title: Self-similar exclusion under local energy estimates
theorems.hypotheses_summary: Self-similar Navier-Stokes solutions satisfying the source's local-energy and stated integrability hypotheses; the published erratum must be consulted for proof-level reuse.
theorems.conclusion_summary: Self-similar solutions in the covered class are trivial, excluding that class as a finite-time blow-up mechanism.
theorems.relation_to_clay: Further narrows the backward self-similar breakdown search space but leaves non-self-similar mechanisms open.
